new.title: Tour Schwerin Castle on its lake island
new.desc: The fairy-tale castle on an island between Schweriner See and Burgsee was rebuilt in historicist style between 1843 and 1857 and is part of the UNESCO World Heritage residence ensemble. Today it houses the state parliament of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and the castle museum with throne room and state apartments.
new.tip: Entry is around 6 euros; check mv-schloesser.de for hours. The seventh floor of the Conti Park garage gives a good photo angle.

new.title: Stroll the baroque Schlossgarten and its canal
new.desc: The Schlossgarten south of the castle follows French baroque design around a cross-shaped canal. It forms part of the castle ensemble and also contains the Orangerie and a grotto from 1852 that shelters bats.
new.tip: Free to walk and open all day; late afternoon light on the castle is best.

new.title: Cross the Burggarten and see the floating meadow
new.desc: The Burggarten is laid out as an English landscape garden with an equestrian statue of Friedrich Franz II and a Bauhaus-style Kreuzgang. In the Burgsee a modern art installation, the floating meadow, provides seating on the water.
new.tip: Reach it via the Alte Brücke from Lennéstraße; it is free to visit.

new.title: Climb the tower of Schwerin Cathedral
new.desc: The brick Gothic cathedral of St. Marien und St. Johannis was completed in 1416 after about 146 years of building. Its neo-Gothic tower of 1893 reaches 117.5 m, the tallest church tower in eastern Germany.
new.tip: The tower viewing platform is reached by a long staircase; opening hours and fees on the cathedral's website.
new.q: Schweriner Dom, Am Dom 4, Altstadt, Schwerin

new.title: Admire the Rathaus and Altstädtischer Markt
new.desc: The market square is framed by the Tudor-style Rathaus, first mentioned in 1351, and the colonnaded Kramsbudengebäude with 14 Doric columns. The 4.5 m Heinrich-der-Löwe-Säule recalls the founder of Schwerin.
new.tip: The Advent Christmas market is held here; cafés on the square make a good pause.

new.title: Find the bull fountain on the Schlachtermarkt
new.desc: Behind the Rathaus arch, the Schlachtermarkt is a small square of historic brick houses. Its fountain shows a bull and bronze figures of market scenes, including a butcher and a musician.
new.tip: Combine with the Altstädtischer Markt; cafés line the square.

new.title: Spot the 1574 half-timbered Domhof
new.desc: A beam inscription dates this half-timbered house at the Domhof to 1574. It once served as a hotel and now houses the state monuments authority. Nearby half-timbered streets such as Buschstraße and Puschkinstraße show other early buildings.
new.tip: Best on foot together with the cathedral, five minutes from the Markt.

new.title: Visit the baroque Schelfkirche in Schelfstadt
new.desc: Consecrated in 1713, St. Nikolai on the Schelf was the first major new church in Mecklenburg after the Reformation. Its crypt holds Duke Friedrich Wilhelm and 17 other members of the ducal house.
new.tip: Check for opening times and crypt tours; the surrounding Schelfstadt streets reward a slow walk.

new.title: See Dutch masters at the Staatliches Museum
new.desc: The museum on Alter Garten holds a renowned collection of Dutch paintings and art from the 16th to 21st century. The 1882 building was extended by new halls and reopened on 30 October 2025 after four years of construction.
new.tip: Admission has been free since reopening for four years; confirm hours on museum-schwerin.de, as some pages still show an old closure notice.
new.q: Staatliches Museum Schwerin, Alter Garten 3, Schwerin

new.title: Walk around the Pfaffenteich promenade
new.desc: The artificial lake beside the old town is lined by grand 19th-century buildings, including the orange Arsenal, the oldest building on the lake. A statue honours street sweeper August Felten (1852 to 1931), a postcard favourite.
new.tip: Sunset along August-Bebel-Straße is the most photogenic; free.

new.title: Watch stone being cut at the Schleifmühle
new.desc: This former water mill at the Faulen See, built around 1700, is a technical museum with a demonstration plant, restored and reopened in 1985. An undershot water wheel drives a saw and a grinding table for stone.
new.tip: Opening days are limited; check the Stadtgeschichts- und Museumsverein before going.

new.title: Step into village life at Freilichtmuseum Mueß
new.desc: The open-air museum for folklore in Schwerin-Mueß preserves farmhouses and village buildings and shows rural life around 1900. It runs events such as the spring market and a hands-on day.
new.tip: Season runs from Easter Saturday to 31 October, roughly 10:00 to 17:00 or 18:00; adults around 5 euros.
new.q: Freilichtmuseum für Volkskunde Schwerin-Mueß, Alte Crivitzer Landstraße 13, Schwerin

new.title: Admire the Mecklenburgisches Staatstheater
new.desc: The neoclassical theatre beside the Alter Garten stages drama, opera, ballet and children's shows. The Alter Garten in front was once a swamp and kitchen garden and now holds the 32 m Siegessäule for the war of 1870 to 1871.
new.tip: Even without a ticket the facade and square are worth a look; free to see from outside.

new.title: Meet giraffes and rhinos at Zoo Schwerin
new.desc: Zoo Schwerin lies on the lake shore beside Zippendorf with more than 140 species and about 1,500 animals. Giraffes and lions are near the entrance, and a savanna holds white rhinos; a Red List Centre covers threatened species.
new.tip: Open daily with seasonal hours (shorter in winter); reachable by boat from the castle pier to Zippendorf.

new.title: Eat Wiener schnitzel at Weinhaus Wöhler
new.desc: Weinhaus Wöhler occupies a historic half-timbered house at Puschkinstraße 26 in the old town. The kitchen is known for a Viennese-style schnitzel with potato and cucumber salad.
new.tip: Book for evenings; pair with a glass from the wine list.

new.title: Order sea bream at Restaurant Lukas
new.desc: Restaurant Lukas at Großer Moor near the cathedral specialises in fish and serves regional Hennings craft beer. Dishes include gilthead sea bream fillet with squid tagliatelle.
new.tip: Mid-range prices; fish plate or the sea bream are the picks. Reviews are mixed, so reserve a table.

new.title: Share a tarte flambée at the Dampfwäscherei
new.desc: The Herzogliche Dampfwäscherei is a restaurant and café in a former ducal steam laundry at Großer Moor. Tarte flambée is a speciality, for example with chanterelles, Serrano ham and parmesan.
new.tip: Come hungry for the tarte flambée; terrace seats in summer.

new.title: Lick soft-serve at ILKA Eis & Heiß
new.desc: ILKA Eis on 2. Enge Straße makes soft ice cream with over 30-year-old Ilka freezer machines from the former GDR. Chocolate-vanilla is the base, with a daily flavour such as blackcurrant-liquorice.
new.tip: Open daily from April to October; cash is safest.
new.q: ILKA Eis & Heiß, 2. Enge Straße 2, Schwerin

new.title: Sip freshly roasted coffee at Rösterei Fuchs
new.desc: Rösterei Fuchs roasts beans from coffee regions worldwide and serves them in the old town. It is regularly listed among the best coffees in Schwerin.
new.tip: Listings give both Am Markt 4 and Enge Straße 2 as addresses; check on arrival. Buy beans to take home.

new.title: Try the checkerboard cake at Café Prag
new.desc: Café Prag in the old town near the castle is known for homemade cakes from its kitchen buffet. A fruit and buttercream checkerboard cake is one of the signature pieces.
new.tip: Visit on the way to or from the castle; cake only, so afternoon is best.

new.title: Drink Schweriner Bock at Zum Freischütz
new.desc: Zum Freischütz on Ziegenmarkt in Schelfstadt is a typical German Kneipe with local beers such as Schweriner Bock and Lübzer. Food is plain and affordable.
new.tip: Cosy atmosphere; try the Bock with a hearty main.

new.title: Go vegan at Angoor in Schelfstadt
new.desc: Angoor on Friedrichstraße serves vegan and vegetarian dishes and is praised for food and ambiance. It is one of the few plant-based kitchens in the city.
new.tip: Friedrichstraße also has Café Friedrichs at no. 2; confirm Angoor is open before a visit.

new.title: Eat Bratkartoffeln at Kartoffelhaus Nr. 1
new.desc: Kartoffelhaus Nr. 1 on Buschstraße in the old town builds its menu around potatoes. Fried potatoes with regional toppings are the classic order.
new.tip: Hearty and good value; popular at lunch.

new.title: Eat by the lake at Strandperle Zippendorf
new.desc: Strandperle sits at Am Strand 14 on the Zippendorf city beach. It is a lakeside snack and drinks spot with views across the Schweriner Innensee.
new.tip: Hours are seasonal and short in autumn and winter; check Facebook first. Best on a summer evening.

new.title: Cruise Schweriner See with the Weiße Flotte
new.desc: The Weiße Flotte sails from the pier by the castle across the Schweriner See, with stops such as Zippendorf and twilight cruises in summer. The lake is the second-largest in northern Germany after the Müritz.
new.tip: Season runs roughly March to October; check the timetable at weisseflotteschwerin.de. Twilight cruises are about 31 euros.
new.q: Weiße Flotte Schwerin, Anleger Schloss, Werderstraße 140, Schwerin

new.title: Walk the Franzosenweg to Zippendorf
new.desc: The Franzosenweg is a shore path of about 3.7 to 4 km from the castle gardens to Zippendorf beach, built by French prisoners of war in 1870 and 1871. It follows the lake with views of the castle.
new.tip: Allow an hour one way and return by boat or bus; free.

new.title: Swim at Zippendorf city beach
new.desc: The Zippendorfer Strand is a sandy beach on the Schweriner Innensee, created about a century ago. It has a playground, beach volleyball and snack bar, and swimming is allowed in designated zones.
new.tip: Free entry; swimming season is summer only.

new.title: Hike the Ostorfer See loop
new.desc: A roughly 12 km circuit around the Ostorfer See starts near Ostorfer Straße and Obotritenring and takes about three hours. It passes woods and lake views close to the city centre.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes; a route description is on ich-geh-wandern.de.

new.title: Sit on the floating meadow in the Burgsee
new.desc: A floating meadow with seating and a modern art installation drifts in the Burgsee beside the castle gardens. It gives a calm view of the castle from the water.
new.tip: Free; best on a dry day, with the Burggarten on the way.

new.title: Ride the ferry across the Pfaffenteich
new.desc: A small passenger ferry crosses the Pfaffenteich, the artificial lake beside the old town. It is a short, cheap way to see the Arsenal and the lakeside villas.
new.tip: Runs in season; fares are a few euros.

new.title: Wander Schelfstadt and its courtyards
new.desc: Schelfstadt holds the largest historic building stock in Schwerin, laid out in the early 18th century. Highlights include the Stadtpalais of 1735 to 1747, the Schelfkirche and the former Schweinemarkt.
new.tip: Look through open gateways at the courtyard gardens; free and around an hour.

new.title: Browse the Schweriner Weihnachtsmarkt
new.desc: The Christmas market fills the Altstädtischer Markt around the Rathaus during Advent. It is the main festive market in the city centre.
new.tip: Visit in the evening when the Markt is lit; expect crowds on weekends.

new.title: Rent a pedal boat or paddleboard on the lake
new.desc: From April to October the Schweriner See offers pedal boats, canoes and stand-up paddling, with designated swimming zones. The Zippendorf shore gives open views toward the castle across the Innensee.
new.tip: Rental availability depends on season and weather; ask at the Zippendorf waterfront.
